Subject: Post-call: Private path performance checklist & next steps

Hi Katie — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items from the discovery call.

Call highlights / performance targets you confirmed:
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms (end-to-end for inference request-response).
- Streaming requirements: client-side streaming for real-time transcription use-case; target sustained bi-directional streams at 200 concurrent streams during peak.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state concurrency target 200 streams, burst to 500 for short windows; expect ~30 tokens/sec per active stream.
- Availability: goal is <1% error rate at target load; graceful fallback to hosted model if private path issues detected.

Private/VPC-specific items we agreed to validate:
1) Network path & egress: provide traceroutes from your app hosts to our edge endpoint (edge-us.redwood.inference). We need both intra-AZ and cross-AZ runs.
2) VPN/Peering details: whether you'll use site-to-site VPN or cloud VPC peering; if peering, confirm CIDR ranges and any overlapping prefixes.
3) BGP / NAT behavior: provide whether you expect asymmetric routing, any NAT gateways, and whether source IPs are preserved.
4) MTU / traffic shaping: confirm if any intermediate devices perform fragmentation; we recommend MTU >= 1400 to avoid TLS fragmentation during streaming.
5) Internal latency budgets: we recommended keeping app->gateway <= 5ms (intra-AZ) and <= 20ms (cross-AZ) to meet end-to-end SLOs.

Attachments: I attached the redwood-private-network-checklist.xlsx with the exact tests we typically run (traceroute, tcpdump, sustained open-stream tests, and a short load plan).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You: send traceroute + any existing network docs (BGP config, VPN topology) by EOD tomorrow.
- Redwood: we'll propose a two-stage canary test plan — low-volume functional (50 concurrent streams), then ramp (200 -> 500) with measurement windows.
- Schedule a 60-minute smoke window next week to run the functional canary.

If anything above doesn't match how you heard it, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll pull together the canary runbook and loop Rishi (SRE) for the instrumentation.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez

Katie — great, thanks for the traceroute. A few technical answers & a proposed minimal test plan:

VPN vs Peering
- VPN: expect additional MTU/NAT effects and slightly higher and potentially variable latency; we will plan tests to surface fragmentation and NAT timeouts.
- Peering: preferred for latency & stability; if you can transition to peering for the pilot that reduces one variable.

Streaming protocol guidance
- Recommended: HTTP/2 gRPC streams (server & client streaming) for the lowest overhead and predictable flow-control behavior.
- WebSockets: supported, and fine for browser clients — note that proxies/load-balancers sometimes buffer; we'll want to validate end-to-end keepalive and idle timeouts.

Ports / TLS / Keepalive
- TLS termination: Redwood expects TLS end-to-end to our edge (443).
- Keepalive: set TCP keepalive to <60s for long-lived streams; if you have an L7 proxy, set idle to >= 180s to avoid premature resets during lull periods.

Minimal canary test plan (what Redwood will execute with you):
1) Functional smoke: 50 concurrent streams, 5-minute window, verify streaming stability and correctness.
2) Sustained: 200 concurrent streams for 10 minutes, capture p50/p95 and error rates.
3) Burst: ramp to 500 concurrent streams for 2 x 2-minute bursts to validate burst-handling and autoscaling behavior.

Metrics we’ll collect:
- End-to-end latency (client request -> first token, and client request -> final token) p50/p95/p999.
- Error rate (5xx, timeouts, connection resets).
- Successful keepalive/stream longevity statistics.

Action items I’ll own: build the runbook and the load profile in our perf harness; request you send us a staging host IP range and a preferred test window (your March 2 pilot looks OK on our side). I’ll also open HS-37491 to track the pilot. Link to our internal runbook: https://redwood-internal.docs/PrivatePathPerfRunbook

Diego
